clinician.trajectory_summary: A 20-year-old gravida 2 para 2 Guatemalan female presented to the emergency department 9 days following uncomplicated full-term vaginal delivery with a 3-day history of nausea, vomiting, abdominal cramping, and profuse non-bloody dark diarrhea (up to 8 times daily). She reported severe lower abdominal pain (8/10) and was found to be febrile and tachycardic on presentation. Physical examination revealed a soft, tender abdomen in all four quadrants on deep palpation with mild guarding and suprapubic tenderness. CT imaging of the abdomen and pelvis demonstrated an enlarged post-gravid uterus with air in the lower uterine segment endometrial cavity, diffuse large bowel wall thickening (suggesting infectious or inflammatory colitis), and a large fluid collection superior to the spleen. Laboratory studies on admission showed decreased hemoglobin and hematocrit, decreased sodium and potassium, elevated platelet count, elevated bands, elevated BUN, and elevated glucose—consistent with systemic infection and sepsis. An exploratory laparotomy was performed on admission day 8, which directly visualized and confirmed diffuse fibrinous peritonitis with no obvious perforation of abdominal viscus. Postoperative cultures returned negative for bacterial growth, possibly due to prior antibiotic treatment. Repeat CT imaging performed one week postoperatively demonstrated significant resolution of the fluid collection superior to the spleen, with only a small, partially loculated collection remaining, indicating clinical improvement with treatment.
